fig1_expansion_pv.svg: The same gas tripling its volume from 0.1 to 0.3 m$^3$ starting at 3 bar, under two idealizations. Held at constant pressure it sweeps the full rectangle, 60.0 kJ (constant_pressure_expansion); expanding isothermally along $pV=$ const the pressure falls as the volume grows and the area shrinks to 33.0 kJ (isothermal_expansion). Both are positive because the system does work on its surroundings — expansion work is energy leaving the system.
fig2_work_vs_ratio.svg: Why the process idealization cannot be waved away. Sweeping the expansion ratio, the constant-pressure work grows linearly in $V_2$ while the isothermal work grows only as $\ln(V_2/V_1)$, so the two diverge steadily: at an eight-fold expansion they are 210.0 kJ against 62.4 kJ, a factor of 3.4. The general quadrature expansion_work applied to the isothermal path returns 62.4 kJ, agreeing with the closed form.
